title: Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem (OQ-04)
description: Kakutani's generalization of Brouwer's fixed point theorem to set-valued (multi-valued) maps, with applications to Nash equilibrium existence.

meta.historicalContext: Shizuo Kakutani (1941) proved this generalization of Brouwer's theorem. John Nash (1950) used it to prove the existence of Nash equilibria, earning the Nobel Prize in Economics (1994). The theorem is essential in mathematical economics (Arrow-Debreu general equilibrium) and optimal control (Filippov's lemma).
meta.assumptions: 2 axiom(s), 0 sorry(s). brouwer_compact_convex_axiom (Brouwer for compact convex sets) and kakutani_fixed_point_axiom (the main Kakutani FPT, requires Brouwer + finite-dimensional approximation/triangulation).

overview.historicalContext: Kakutani's fixed point theorem (1941) is one of the most consequential generalizations in mathematics. It extends Brouwer's theorem from continuous functions to upper hemicontinuous set-valued maps (correspondences). John Nash's 1950 proof of equilibrium existence in non-cooperative games -- for which he received the 1994 Nobel Prize -- relies essentially on Kakutani's theorem. The Arrow-Debreu proof of general economic equilibrium (1954) also uses it.
overview.problemStatement: **Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem**: Let S be a nonempty compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $F: S \to 2^S$ be an upper hemicontinuous correspondence with nonempty, convex, closed values. Then F has a fixed point: $\exists x^* \in S, x^* \in F(x^*)$.
overview.text: Kakutani's generalization of Brouwer to set-valued maps, with applications to Nash equilibrium.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization builds in 8 parts: (1) Define correspondences as structures with nonempty/closed values and maps-to constraints. (2) Define upper hemicontinuity via the Berge (1959) neighborhood formulation. (3) Axiomatize Kakutani FPT with detailed proof sketch. (4) Prove Kakutani reduces to Brouwer for singleton correspondences. (5) Prove 1D Kakutani using IVT (fully proved, no axioms). (6) Build correspondence algebra (constant, identity). (7) Develop Nash equilibrium framework: mixed strategies are compact, convex, closed. (8) Prove UHC properties for constant maps and continuous images.
keyInsights: **Singleton reduction**: When F(x) = {f(x)} for a continuous f, Kakutani's conditions reduce to Brouwer's. This is proved constructively.
**1D Kakutani via IVT**: For interval correspondences F(x) = [l(x), u(x)] on [0,1], the IVT on g(x) = u(x) - x gives a fixed point. This is the only fully proved case.
**Mixed strategies are compact convex**: The simplex {sigma | sigma_i >= 0, sum = 1} is closed (intersection of halfspaces and hyperplane), bounded, hence compact.
**Upper hemicontinuity generalizes continuity**: A continuous function f induces a UHC singleton correspondence {f(x)} -- the preimage characterization reduces to ordinary continuity.
prerequisites: Convex analysis: convex sets, convex combinations
Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem (for general case)

sections.title: Correspondences (Set-Valued Maps)
sections.summary: Defines the `Correspondence` structure and fixed points for set-valued maps.

sections.title: Upper Hemicontinuity
sections.summary: Defines upper hemicontinuity (Berge 1959) and proves continuous functions induce UHC singleton correspondences.

sections.title: The Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Brouwer for compact convex sets and Kakutani FPT with detailed classical proof sketch.

sections.title: Single-Valued Reduction
sections.summary: Proves Kakutani generalizes Brouwer: singleton correspondences satisfy Kakutani's hypotheses, and fixed points correspond to classical fixed points.

sections.title: 1D Kakutani via IVT
sections.summary: Fully proves the 1D Kakutani theorem for interval correspondences F(x) = [l(x), u(x)] using the Intermediate Value Theorem.

sections.title: Nash Equilibrium Framework
sections.summary: Defines finite games, mixed strategies, and proves mixed strategy spaces are compact convex sets -- the prerequisites for Nash equilibrium existence via Kakutani.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem, its relationship to Brouwer, and its application to Nash equilibrium. 0 sorries, 2 axioms (Brouwer for compact convex sets and Kakutani FPT). The 1D case is fully proved via IVT.
conclusion.implications: Kakutani's theorem is the bridge between pure topology and applied mathematics. It transforms Brouwer's abstract existence result into a tool for economics (equilibrium existence), game theory (Nash equilibria), and control theory (differential inclusions). The formalization demonstrates this bridge explicitly.
openQuestions: Can the main Kakutani FPT be proved from Brouwer using only Mathlib's current topology?
Can the Nash equilibrium existence theorem be fully formalized using the Kakutani axiom?
What is needed to extend to infinite-dimensional Kakutani (Glicksberg-Fan theorem)?
